grades.question: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.

expected.answer: Invaders do 3 Damage simultaneously to land and Dahan, adding one Blight, killing one Dahan and damaging the other by 1. The surviving Dahan still deals 2 Damage, destroying the Town and generating 1 Fear. Dahan do not absorb/prevent land damage; partial Dahan damage clears at Time Passes.

observed.answer: Invaders deal 3 Damage (Town 2 plus Explorer 1) separately and simultaneously to land and Dahan. The land takes at least 2, so add one Blight. The Dahan take 3: one dies and the other takes 1 Damage. The survivor counterattacks for 2 Damage; destroying the Town earns 1 Fear.

evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. **Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

grades.question: How do Damage, Destroy, Remove and Replace differ for Fear and survival? Can Damage from separate normal Powers combine, does Damage normally hurt Dahan, and does replacement erase prior Damage?

expected.answer: Damage normally means to Invaders only, distributed as chosen in target land; can combine within turn, immediately destroying pieces at Damage >= Health. Destroying Town/City produces 1/2 Fear in addition to explicit Fear. Remove/Replace generate none automatically; Replace retains prior Damage and may cause destruction if Damage meets new Health (then destruction Fear applies). Surviving Damage clears at Time Passes. Dahan are harmed by Powers only if explicitly stated. An outright Destroy instruction eliminates its specified piece regardless of its Damage or Health. Remove likewise takes the specified piece off the board without requiring Damage to reach Health. Replace removes the original and puts the specified replacement in its place.

grades.question: Can Mantle of Dread choose one of target Spirit’s lands with only an Explorer even when another land has Explorer and Town? Can Tidal Boon Push Dahan from a land without a Town, and does its if-Dahan-are-pushed clause apply to later unrelated Pushes?

expected.answer: Yes to both land choices: target Spirit chooses one of its lands and does as much as possible there. Tidal Boon’s clause applies only to its own Push, not later unrelated Pushes.

observed.answer: Target Spirit chooses one of its lands and does as much there as possible, even if another land would allow more. Thus both stated Pushes are allowed without a Town. Tidal Boon’s “if Dahan are pushed” applies only to that Power’s own Push.

evidence.text: - **Spirit-targeting Powers:** When the target Spirit selects “one of their lands,” it chooses the land and does as much there as possible, even if another of its lands would permit more instructions. Tidal Boon's “if Dahan are pushed” clause applies only to that Power's own Push. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move Dahan pushed to its Ocean by that use to **any Coastal land**, including a nonadjacent one, instead of Drowning them. Ocean chooses; this alternative is optional. [Original core card text] Spirit-targeting Fear without a specified land has no particular land for **Dread Apparitions**. grades.question: Two Dahan Move (not Gather or Push) from one land to another. How many of Thunderspeaker’s Presence may accompany them? If they move into an Ocean made legal by Ocean’s rule, may Presence accompany them there?

expected.answer: Up to one Presence per moved Dahan, so two, with them. Generic Move qualifies as well as Gather/Push. Presence may accompany them into a legally targeted Ocean via the Power/Ocean-rule interaction.

observed.answer: Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move, so two Dahan can carry two Presence. They can accompany Dahan into Ocean when a legal Power permits it.

evidence.text: - **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. Finish the Ravage, cascades and counterattack before this triggered loss. [Core: .bu6oc6l, .bu6oc73, .bu6ofsi]

- **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. grades.question: When Ocean exchanges already Drowned Invaders for Energy, does it value their modified current Health, or their printed Health? Do temporary and permanent Health modifiers change that exchange value?

expected.answer: Use unmodified printed Health and ignore all Health modifiers, temporary or permanent, for the Energy exchange.
source_refs: /home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/batches/2026-11-05-batch-002957/source-preflight/spirit-island/living-faq-core-game.txt | FAQ .9v5ka9g: ignore all Invader Health modifiers when trading | SHA256 874741b896dd163568a7e33ee4341fe7b38db9a2834185d272d662573de3679e | Unicode chars 195463:196249 | passage SHA256 e36aa1d9f57b7411f65d529a29f724d99af75a3eb49988d7b2ce29fc5dbd321a

requested_parts: Ocean exchange printed vs modified health
observed.answer: Use printed Health and ignore Health modifiers.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. observed.answer: They deal Ravage Damage simultaneously with Invaders, and a Dahan killed in that exchange still contributes its Damage. No second later counterattack.

evidence.text: - **Triggered effects:** “After” effects resolve after the whole originating action, not after each instruction within a Power. A triggered effect cannot trigger itself, even indirectly. Separately repeated instances can trigger one another, but neither can recur within its own chain. **Vengeance of the Dead** uses this timing; its corrected base text grants 3 Fear and, after an effect destroys Towns/Cities/Dahan in target land, deals 1 Damage per such piece destroyed. Its threshold may send that Damage into adjacent lands, while the original target remains the land whose qualifying destruction triggers it. The triggered effect still belongs to the Spirit that used Vengeance: if Bringer used it, its later Damage follows To Dream a Thousand Deaths even when another Spirit's action caused the triggering destruction. observed.answer: Any fitting arrangement is legal; bottom-to-bottom is only shown as an example.

evidence.text:
1. **Island:** Randomly choose one Island Board per Spirit and join the balanced sides using the layout for that Spirit count. [CORE pp.6–7; FAQ .7w4g8pg]

   | Spirits / boards | Balanced Island layout |
   | --- | --- |
   | 1 | One board. |
   | 2 | Any fitting arrangement is legal. The rulebook shows bottom-to-bottom, with Oceans facing opposite outer corners. |

requested_parts: Trade stored Invaders between actions later Spirit Phase
observed.answer: Yes. Ocean may exchange stored Invaders between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. requested_parts: Nightmare Fear for same Town during one Tsunami use
observed.answer: No. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once, even if later threshold Damage reaches it again in another land.

evidence.text:
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally. Apply these results separately to each would-be-destroyed Invader; the Fear result does not itself grant movement:

  | Would-be-destroyed Invader | Fear | Movement from this special rule |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Explorer | 0 | Push it. |
  | Town | 2 | Push it. |
  | City | 5 | No Push. |

  No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. grades.question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?

expected.answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.

requested_parts: whether the second placement can use the first as range origin
observed.answer: Yes; placements resolve sequentially and the new disk may be the next origin. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either track. Use each track’s highest uncovered number independently; do not add Energy and Card Plays together.

evidence.text: - **Add Presence:** Choose a legal land within the shown maximum Range of your existing Presence. Take the leftmost remaining disk from either Presence track and add it there. With multiple placements, resolve them sequentially: a newly placed disk may be the origin for the next. You may instead **reposition any of your island Presence**, even with track disks remaining: first measure range and select the destination using existing Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take a disk from anywhere on the island. This is still an Add Presence instruction, not a Move instruction. Destroyed Presence cannot be used unless explicitly permitted.

**Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

evidence.text: **Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. grades.question: Can Wrap in Wings of Sunlight grant Defend if it moves zero Dahan? Can it count as movement when Dahan are moved to their current land if otherwise permitted? Can Blazing Renewal do threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence to add?

expected.answer: Zero Move grants no Defend because there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their own land counts as Move when not otherwise restricted. Blazing Renewal cannot deal threshold Damage without restoring destroyed Presence; that land is the placement land.

requested_parts: Wrap Defend with zero moved Dahan
observed.answer: Wrap grants no Defend if zero Dahan move because there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their current land can count as Move if permitted. Blazing Renewal cannot deal threshold Damage if it adds no destroyed Presence: “that land” means the land where Presence is added.

evidence.text: - **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Each destination receives Defend 2 for each Dahan this Power Pushes into it. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

grades.question: Can Mantle of Dread choose one of target Spirit’s lands with only an Explorer even when another land has Explorer and Town? Can Tidal Boon Push Dahan from a land without a Town, and does its if-Dahan-are-pushed clause apply to later unrelated Pushes?

expected.answer: Yes to both land choices: target Spirit chooses one of its lands and does as much as possible there. Tidal Boon’s clause applies only to its own Push, not later unrelated Pushes.

requested_parts: Mantle target land with only Explorer
Tidal Boon Push from no-Town land
observed.answer: The target Spirit chooses one of its lands and does as much as possible there, so Mantle can Push an Explorer from a land without a Town. Tidal Boon can Push Dahan from a land without a Town; its conditional clause concerns only that Power’s own Push.

evidence.text: - **Spirit-targeting Powers:** When the target Spirit selects “one of their lands,” it chooses the land and does as much there as possible, even if another of its lands would permit more instructions. Thus **Mantle of Dread** may Push an Explorer from a land without a Town, and **Tidal Boon** may Push Dahan from a land without a Town. Tidal Boon's “if Dahan are pushed” clause applies only to that Power's own Push. When Ocean uses Tidal Boon, Ocean may move Dahan pushed to its Ocean by that use to **any Coastal land**, including a nonadjacent one, instead of Drowning them. Ocean chooses; this alternative is optional. [Original core card text] Spirit-targeting Fear without a specified land has no particular land for **Dread Apparitions**. evidence.text: - **Thunderspeaker:** Presence may accompany each moved Dahan, including generic Move as well as Gather/Push; two Dahan can carry two Presence. **Sworn to Victory** triggers after an entire single-land Ravage for each Dahan destroyed there: destroy one of Thunderspeaker's Presence within Range 1 per Dahan, even if no Blight was added. - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. grades.question: On a board with Ocean’s Presence only in a Coastal land, can a Power Push Invaders into that board’s Ocean to Drown? Must Ocean have Presence in the Ocean itself, and can Fear Cards or Invader actions ordinarily use it as a land?

expected.answer: Yes, any of Ocean’s Presence on board activates Ocean In Play; no Ocean disk required. Ocean is Coastal Wetland for Powers and Blight, not normal Fear/Invader actions. Humans moved there are Drowned after originating movement action.

requested_parts: Drowning on board with Ocean Presence elsewhere
observed.answer: Yes, Ocean Drowns pieces moved into Ocean on a board with any Ocean Presence; it need not be in the Ocean itself. Ocean is not normally a land for Fear Cards or Invader actions.

evidence.text: - **Ocean's Hungry Grasp:** On a board with any of Ocean's Presence, the Ocean is a Coastal Wetland for **Powers and Blight**, not for normal Growth, Invader actions or Fear Cards. Powers and Special Rules can measure Range through it as a land. [Core: range-through-ocean] Powers can target it and move Invaders/Dahan into it; Blight can cascade into it. Other Spirits' Presence may end up there via a legal Power, including Thunderspeaker accompanying moved Dahan. You can measure Growth placement Range **from existing Ocean Presence**, although normal Growth cannot add to the Ocean just by treating it as a Coastal Wetland. The Growth group explicitly adding two Presence in **any Ocean** can place them in any board's Ocean, even a board where Ocean has no Presence, without a numeric Range requirement. This Growth group places in Oceans only; it does not place Presence Inland. Its other group's Range-1 **Coastal land** placement does not permit placing in the Ocean. Other placement must respect Ocean's land-type restriction unless expressly ignored (e.g., **Indomitable Claim** for Inland Presence). [Core: .bu6odcf, .7w4gef8, .9v5kf36, .9v5ka9o, .9v5kc4i, When-OHG-is-in-play-can-other-pieces-end-up-in-the-Ocean]

- **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. [Core: .7w4g8qy, .9v5kbka, .7w4g8pb, .9v5ka9g, .7w4g8r4, .9v5kfqb, .9v5kfqs, .7w4gdtl]

Each balanced board has eight lands, two each of Jungle, Mountain, Sands and Wetland. Lands are adjacent if they touch by border **or corner**, including across boards. Ocean is not normally a land or in play. Only lands touching a printed Ocean are Coastal; the other outside edges are cliffs, not coast. Other lands are Inland.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. requested_parts: when stored Invaders can be exchanged for Energy
observed.answer: Ocean may exchange stored Invaders between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards; does not need to wait for Drowning or Gain Energy.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. grades.question: Green chooses its Reclaim-and-gain-Power Growth group. Does it also perform the separate ALWAYS Add Presence to Jungle/Wetland, or must it choose between that addition and Reclaim?

expected.answer: It also performs the separate ALWAYS Add Presence instruction. Green resolves that mandatory instruction in addition to its selected Reclaim-and-gain-Power group.
source_refs: /home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/batches/2026-11-05-batch-002957/source-preflight/spirit-island/original-spirit-panels/green-front.png | native original-core panel | SHA256 c909ca5d89faeadd770b71c830351afb161db2c2c215e58ed960d82291498391 | primary native printed face

requested_parts: performing Green's Always placement alongside Reclaim/gain group
observed.answer: Yes. Green’s separate Always Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including Reclaim/gain Power; it is not an either/or choice.

evidence.text: - **A Spread of Rampant Green:** **Choke the Land with Green** is optional (some printings omit “may”). Each use skips just that Ravage or Build action and costs one of Green's Presence in its Sacred Site there. A later Build needs a fresh decision and another disk: starting with three, Green may skip the Ravage, retain a two-disk Sacred Site, then skip the Build and end with one disk. **Steady Regeneration**'s Healthy/Blighted test refers to the Blight Card, not Blight in the destination land. When adding Presence via Growth, Green may use destroyed disks instead of track disks even while disks remain on tracks: this is free while Healthy, or costs 1 Energy per destroyed disk while Blighted. This permission applies only to Growth; an ordinary Power needs its own explicit destroyed-Presence permission. Green's separate **Always** Range-2 Jungle/Wetland placement is additional to its one chosen Growth group, including when it chooses Reclaim/gain a Power. It still chooses only one of the optional groups. Growth instructions from multiple options can be ordered together, so a gained Power may inform the mandatory placement. Its explicit regeneration can use destroyed Presence; ordinary placement cannot. [Core: .9v5kc2v, .7w4g8r1, .bu6oegz, .7w4g8nv]
